title: Treat Matroska cover image streams as attached pictures
summary: Classify Matroska cover image streams as attached pictures when ffprobe exposes them as video streams with image attachment tags but no attached_pic disposition.
reason: Ascendance of a Bookworm S03 files include a single H.264 episode stream plus cover.jpg as an MJPEG image attachment. MediaInfo reports VideoCount=1 and ImageCount=1, but the existing ffprobe inventory counted the tagged cover image as a second real video stream and blocked encode with SOURCE_VIDEO_STREAMS_UNVETTED.
behavior_before: Get-SourceVideoStreamInventory relied on ffprobe disposition.attached_pic to separate cover art from real video. When ffprobe omitted that JSON disposition for a Matroska cover image, the MJPEG cover stream was counted as real video and encode/remux failed closed as multi-video.
behavior_after: The video inventory probe asks ffprobe for filename/mimetype stream tags and treats image attachments as attached pictures when either attached_pic is set or the stream carries image mimetype/filename evidence. True multi-real-video sources still fail closed.
manual_validation: Live read-only Test-SourceVideoStreamPublishPolicy probe against copied failure artifact returned Allowed=true, RealVideoStreamCount=1, AttachedPicCount=1
Read-only ffmpeg mapping check confirmed -map 0:V copies only stream 0:0 while -map 0:v includes cover stream 0:5
ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-MediaVerificationSafetyChecks.ps1 - passed after final packet summary regeneration
rollback_plan: Revert the Test-SourceVideoStreamAttachedPicture helper/tag-based classification and the tagged-cover regression case, then rerun Invoke-MediaVerificationSafetyChecks.ps1.
notes:
SOURCE_VIDEO_STREAMS_UNVETTED reproduced on Matroska cover art: ffprobe JSON reports cover.jpg as mjpeg video with image/jpeg tags but no attached_pic disposition; ffmpeg -map 0:V excludes it.
Old failure markers remain historical UI state; clear the marker and rerun affected sources after updating the pipeline code.
